components.name: registry-key
components.description: Key of an entry in the auths map: the registry host.

components.name: auth
components.description: Standard base64 of username, a colon and password (docker/cli encodeAuth).

components.name: store-references
components.description: credsStore (one helper suffix) and credHelpers (map of registry to helper suffix).

claims.statement: docker/cli's config file type has an auths map of per-registry AuthConfig entries (username, password, auth, serveraddress, identitytoken, registrytoken), a credsStore string and a credHelpers map.

sources.supports: ConfigFile: AuthConfigs map[string]types.AuthConfig `json:"auths"`; CredentialsStore string `json:"credsStore,omitempty"`; CredentialHelpers map[string]string `json:"credHelpers,omitempty"`.
AuthConfig struct with Username, Password, Auth, ServerAddress, IdentityToken and RegistryToken fields.

claims.statement: The auth value is the standard base64 encoding of the username, a colon and the password; saving the file encodes auth this way and blanks out the original username and password fields, and loading decodes it by splitting at the first colon.

sources.supports: encodeAuth: authStr := authConfig.Username + ":" + authConfig.Password, then base64.StdEncoding; decodeAuth cuts the decoded text at the first colon.
SaveToWriter: encode and save the authstring, while blanking out the original fields.

claims.statement: Docker documents that without a configured credential store it stores credentials in config.json in a base64-encoded format and that this is less secure than a credential store.

sources.supports: If you don't configure a credential store, Docker stores credentials in the config.json file in a base64-encoded format. This method is less secure than configuring and using a credential store.

claims.statement: credsStore holds the suffix of a helper program (everything after docker-credential-) and credHelpers maps registry domains to such suffixes; both name a program, and the credentials live in the external store.

sources.supports: You need to specify the credential store in $HOME/.docker/config.json to tell the Docker Engine to use it. The value of the config property should be the suffix of the program to use (i.e. everything after docker-credential-).

Credential helpers are specified in a similar way to credsStore, but allow for multiple helpers to be configured at a time. Keys specify the registry domain, and values specify the suffix of the program to use.

claims.statement: AuthConfig describes identitytoken as used "to authenticate the user and get an access token for the registry" and registrytoken as "a bearer token to be sent to a registry". This run authors no fixture for either.

sources.supports: IdentityToken is used to authenticate the user and get an access token for the registry. RegistryToken is a bearer token to be sent to a registry.

openQuestions.question: Which fields does a current docker login write when no credential store is configured (auth only, or also identitytoken)? The source read shows save-time blanking of username and password only.
